brief: A tool caddy with a carry handle and divided bins for screws and bits.

requirements.evidence: Two adjacent hex bases (piece:0,0,0;full and piece:1,0,0;full) with solid top covers forming a 2-cell tray base, bins sitting on level 0 inside the perimeter
handle:0,0,0;top bridging covers on cell 0,0,0 with supporting inserts, centered for two-handed carry of the 2-cell caddy

requirements.requirement: Divided bins for screws and small parts
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 each with 3 compartments (6 total); staged with heap-screws-div3, heap-nuts-div3, heap-standoffs-div3 representing screws/bits separation
Remaining compartments staged with screwdriver, hexkey-set, pliers as representative bits/hand tools; compartment size ~44x124mm fits typical bit cases

finish.summary: Built a 2-cell portable caddy on solid top covers with two full-height divided bins (hex-bin-full-div3 x2 = 6 compartments) and a central top handle. Staged with screws, nuts, standoffs and hand tools to show screws-and-bits organization. Caps and joint bolt applied.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
